C0.quote: computing the probability of winning in an election where voter attendance
C0.note: Computational aspects of voting rules under uncertain voter attendance.

C1.quote: it is computationally hard (#P-hard) for various other rules
C1.note: Control problems (CCAV/CCAUV) are used only as auxiliary problems in hardness reductions, not as analyses of strategic behaviour.

C2.1.quote: A voting profile T = (𝑇1, . . . ,𝑇𝑛 ) consists of 𝑛 linear orders

C2.2.quote: 𝑇𝑖 is the ranking of (i.e., linear order over) 𝐶 by 𝑣𝑖

C2.3.quote: each voter has an individual preference, namely ordering over the candidates

C2.4.quote: a voting rule is applied to the preference profile
C2.4.note: Preferences/rankings are fed directly to the rule. There is no statement about reporting.

C3.1.quote: voters participate by being drawn randomly from 𝑉
C3.1.note: Only attendance is random. No misreporting is considered.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare or similar notions are used for voters.

VOT.quote_behav: she casts a vote with probability 𝑝𝑖
VOT.note: Attendance is exogenous and random. Votes are the voters' orders.

ORG.note: CCAV/CCAUV control problems appear only as auxiliary decision/counting problems in reductions. No controlling agent acts in the main model.
